Note::TexAccessor::graphics_tags¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::graphics_tags() const

Retain Graphic Locations As Text¶

graphics_tags() rewrites each complete \includegraphics[options]{path} call as [graphic:path]. It exists for pipelines that cannot render or load an asset but must retain where the source referred to one. The method performs no filesystem access, path normalization, existence check, image decoding, or option interpretation. The path is authored text, not a resolved resource.

The command name is matched exactly. Its optional group and required path group are parsed with balanced delimiters, so nested braces in an option or path do not truncate the call. Options disappear from the result; whitespace and text around the call remain. Escaped commands, longer names such as \includegraphicsx, and incomplete option or path groups are preserved verbatim because the method cannot identify a complete replaceable construct.

Choose includes() when paths should be extracted into a lane-aware TokenBatch, input_tags() when input, include, and graphic directives all need visible tags, or strip_graphics() when graphic directives and figure-family environments should be removed.

The result is a newly allocated Text Note with the receiver’s shape. Empty cells stay empty, and applying the operation again is stable because generated tags contain no TeX command. Undefined state propagates; defined non-Text input rejects. The balanced scanner is linear in source bytes and uses nesting-depth storage for the current option or path.

Example 1: Balanced Options, Nested Paths, And Boundaries¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \includegraphics[width={.5\textwidth}]{plots/{loss}.pdf} B)",
    R"(\\includegraphics{escaped} \includegraphicsx{long})",
    R"(\includegraphics[width=2cm]{unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().graphics_tags() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A [graphic:plots/{loss}.pdf] B", "\\\\includegraphics{escaped} \\includegraphicsx{long}", "\\includegraphics[width=2cm]{unfinished"]

Example 2: Batched Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\includegraphics{a.png})", "plain",
                             R"(x \includegraphics{b.pdf} y)", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().graphics_tags() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["[graphic:a.png]", "plain"],
  ["x [graphic:b.pdf] y", ""]
]

Example 3: Undefined State, Dtype, And Idempotence¶

const auto once = pluss::make_note(R"(\includegraphics{plot.pdf})")
                      .tex().graphics_tags();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent="
          << ((once == once.tex().graphics_tags()).all().bool_item())
          << " undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().graphics_tags().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1})
      .tex().graphics_tags();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "graphics tags Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

idempotent=true undefined=false
graphics tags Int64: rejected
